renders.prompt: Explain the argument of this song as if to a bright 10-year-old. Short words. Concrete images. No jargon, no Sanskrit terms, no meta-commentary.

paragraphs.text: Your body is a temple and you are the god who lives there. Sweep out the dusty old thinking, and pray the way that says I am Him. At the door stands the elephant god — everyone from demons to gods bows to him, and he loves giving exactly the gift you wished for.

Next to him stands the Boy, worshipped by heroes, yoginis, and perfected saints — he lifts the pain of humble learners. Then the spotless true teacher: by his mind's strength your whole world lights up as God's road.

In your heart sits blissful Bhairava, made of pure knowing — and your senses, like goddesses, keep offering him everything they taste and touch and see. Beside him his queen Bhairavī, made of pure noticing — she lights up the world and turns it over and over, and she never stops.
From the east, Brāhmī — your power to know — lays down flowers of sure decisions. From the southeast, mother Śāmbhavī — your I-maker — lays down flowers of I-ness itself.

paragraphs.text: Your body is the temple, you are the god posted inside. Take out the trash-thinking, pray the I-am-Him prayer. Door guy one: elephant god, demons and gods both pay respects, hands out wished-for gifts on request.
Door guy two: the Boy — heroes, yoginis, siddhas all at his feet; humble folks' pain gets deleted. Then the actual teacher, spotless: his mind-strength makes your whole world glow Śiva's-path.
Heart HQ: bliss-Bhairava, consciousness-built, showered with sense-offerings nonstop. Next to him Bhairavī, noticing-built — world goes up, world gets chewed, she never sleeps on it.
East side: Brāhmī, your intellect, dropping resolve-flowers. Southeast: Śāmbhavī-mom, your I-maker, dropping I-flowers.
